headline: Scotland's Wind Farm Proves 99.9% Turbine Recycling Is Possible
meta_description: Scotland's first commercial wind farm has recycled or reused 99.9% of decommissioned turbine parts, addressing a major criticism of wind power sustainability.
summary_short: Scotland's pioneering wind farm has successfully recycled or reused nearly all of its decommissioned turbine components, including blades—a major win for renewable energ…
body:
Scotland's first commercial wind farm has recycled or reused 99.9% of its decommissioned turbine parts, proving that end-of-life wind infrastructure needn't become waste.

The achievement directly addresses one of wind power's most persistent criticisms: that massive turbine blades are too difficult to recycle and end up in landfills. By successfully handling even these challenging components, the farm demonstrates a viable path forward for the industry as it scales globally.

This milestone suggests that with proper planning and investment, wind farms can operate within a genuine circular economy, turning decommissioning into an opportunity rather than an environmental liability. As more turbines reach the end of their operational lives worldwide, Scotland's example offers both technical proof and practical hope.
quick_facts: Scotland's first commercial wind farm recycled 99.9% of turbine parts
Even turbine blades were successfully recycled or reused
Addresses major sustainability criticism of wind power industry
